component.name: ssh
component.title: SSH
component.description: Execute commands on remote hosts using SSH.
component.label: file

timeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the component waits for each step of setting up the session: the connection, the authentication and the opening of the channel, unless channelOpenTimeout is set. It does not limit how long the command runs.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

pollCommand.label: consumer
pollCommand.description: The command that the consumer runs on the SSH server at each poll. The consumer needs it, as each poll fails without it. Some servers need the command to end with a newline, which is written %0A in an endpoint URI.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

authTimeout.label: advanced
authTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds that Apache MINA SSHD allows for the authentication before it closes the session. If 0 or less, its default of 2 minutes applies. The timeout option also limits how long the component waits for the authentication.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

channelOpenTimeout.label: advanced
channelOpenTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the component waits for the channel that runs the command to open. If 0 or less, the timeout option applies.

channelType.label: advanced
channelType.description: The type of SSH channel that runs the command: exec runs it as a single command, and shell writes it to an interactive shell and reads the output up to the shellPrompt text. The endpoint fails to start with another value.

clientBuilder.label: advanced
clientBuilder.description: To use a custom org.apache.sshd.client.ClientBuilder to create the SSH client, for example to set a ServerKeyVerifier. The producer and the consumer each create a client with it when they start, and the options of this endpoint that are set are applied over its settings.

compressions.label: advanced
compressions.description: A comma-separated list of the compression algorithms that the client proposes, in order of preference, for example zlib,none. If not set, the client uses no compression.

configuration.label: advanced
configuration.description: The shared configuration of the endpoints: each endpoint starts from a copy of it.

connectTimeout.label: advanced
connectTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the socket connection to the server may take. If 0 or less, the default of Apache MINA SSHD, 1 minute, applies. The timeout option also limits how long the component waits for the connection.

heartbeatInterval.label: advanced
heartbeatInterval.description: The interval in milliseconds at which the client sends keep-alive requests to the server while a command runs. If 0 or less, no keep-alive requests are sent.

heartbeatReplyMaxWait.label: advanced
heartbeatReplyMaxWait.description: The number of keep-alive requests without reply after which the client closes the session, when heartbeatInterval is set. If 0 or less, the default of Apache MINA SSHD applies.

idleTimeout.label: advanced
idleTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds after which Apache MINA SSHD closes a session without traffic. The session is open while a command runs. The default, 10 minutes, is the default of Apache MINA SSHD. If 0 or less, the session has no idle timeout.

shellPrompt.label: advanced
shellPrompt.description: The text that the shell prompt ends with, which channelType=shell needs: the endpoint fails to start without it. The component reads the output of the shell until it ends with this text, before and after it writes the command, and the message body is the text between the first and the last line break of that output.

sleepForShellPrompt.label: advanced
sleepForShellPrompt.description: The time in milliseconds between two reads of the shell output while the component waits for the shellPrompt text, with channelType=shell.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

certResource.label: security
certResource.description: The resource with the private key for public key authentication, in OpenSSH or PEM format, for example classpath:id_ed25519 or file:/home/camel/.ssh/id_ed25519. When set, it is used instead of keyPairProvider, and the password option and the CamelSshPassword header are not used.

certResourcePassword.label: security
certResourcePassword.description: The passphrase of the private key in certResource, when that key is encrypted.

ciphers.label: security
ciphers.description: A comma-separated list of the ciphers that the client proposes, in order of preference, for example aes256-ctr,aes128-ctr. It replaces the default list of Apache MINA SSHD. Names that are not known are skipped with a warning.

failOnUnknownHost.label: security
failOnUnknownHost.description: Whether to reject a server whose host has no entry without a marker in knownHostsResource. When false, such a server is accepted and a warning is logged. A server whose host has such entries is always rejected when none of them lists the key it presents, and so is a key listed in a matching entry with the revoked marker. This option has no effect when knownHostsResource is not set.

kex.label: security
kex.description: A comma-separated list of the key exchange algorithms that the client proposes, in order of preference, for example mlkem768x25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256. It replaces the default list of Apache MINA SSHD, which already proposes the post-quantum hybrid algorithms. Names that are not known are skipped with a warning.

keyPairProvider.label: security
keyPairProvider.description: The org.apache.sshd.common.keyprovider.KeyPairProvider that gives the key pair for public key authentication. It is not used when certResource is set, and when it is used, the password option and the CamelSshPassword header are not.

keyType.label: security
keyType.description: The key type of the key pair to use from certResource or keyPairProvider, for example ssh-rsa, ssh-ed25519 or ecdsa-sha2-nistp256. If not set, the first key pair is used.

knownHostsResource.label: security
knownHostsResource.description: The resource of a file in the OpenSSH known_hosts format, such as file:/etc/camel/known_hosts, that the server host key is verified against. It is read at each connection, and a resource or a line that cannot be read makes every connection fail. When not set, the server host key is not verified and any server is accepted, unless clientBuilder sets a ServerKeyVerifier, which this option replaces when it is set.

macs.label: security
macs.description: A comma-separated list of the message authentication code (MAC) algorithms that the client proposes, in order of preference, for example hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256. It replaces the default list of Apache MINA SSHD. Names that are not known are skipped with a warning.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for password authentication, which is used only when neither certResource nor keyPairProvider is set. The CamelSshPassword header replaces it for the producer.

signatures.label: security
signatures.description: A comma-separated list of the signature algorithms that the client supports, in order of preference, for example ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-512. It replaces the default list of Apache MINA SSHD. Names that are not known are skipped with a warning.

username.label: security
username.description: The user name to log in with. The CamelSshUsername header replaces it for the producer.

CamelSshUsername.description: The user name that the producer logs in with, instead of the username option.

CamelSshPassword.description: The password that the producer uses for password authentication, instead of the password option. It is not used when certResource or keyPairProvider is set.

CamelSshStderr.description: The standard error of the command, as an InputStream.

CamelSshExitValue.description: The exit status of the command. By convention, a value other than 0 means that the command failed, but the exchange does not fail for it. With channelType=shell it is usually null, as the shell is still running when the output is read.

consumerOut.description: The standard output of the pollCommand as a stream, with the exit value and the standard error in the CamelSshExitValue and CamelSshStderr headers

producerIn.description: The command to run, as text: bytes, a stream or a file are read as text. A Map or a POJO is sent as its toString(): build the command as text first. No body fails

producerOut.description: The standard output of the command as a stream, with the exit value and the standard error in the CamelSshExitValue and CamelSshStderr headers; an exit value that is not 0 does not fail the exchange. Convert it to text to read it more than once

host.description: The host name or IP address of the SSH server. When the .ssh/config file in the home directory of the user has an entry for this host, the client connects to the HostName of that entry.

port.description: The port of the SSH server.

timeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the component waits for each step of setting up the session: the connection, the authentication and the opening of the channel, unless channelOpenTimeout is set. It does not limit how long the command runs.

sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.label: consumer
sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

pollStrategy.label: consumer,advanced
pollStrategy.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

backoffErrorThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffErrorThreshold.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffIdleThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffIdleThreshold.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffMultiplier.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffMultiplier.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

greedy.label: consumer,scheduler
greedy.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

healthCheckMaxPollDuration.label: consumer,scheduler
healthCheckMaxPollDuration.description: How long a poll may run before the health check of the consumer reports DOWN. The health check is otherwise based on the polls that are done, so it stays UP while a poll hangs, for example on a read without timeout from a connection that went silent. A poll includes routing the messages it polled, so set this above the longest poll you expect. The poll is not interrupted. The value is in millis (not affected by timeUnit). The default 0 turns this off.

initialDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
initialDelay.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

repeatCount.label: consumer,scheduler
repeatCount.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

runLoggingLevel.label: consumer,scheduler
runLoggingLevel.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

scheduledExecutorService.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduledExecutorService.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

scheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduler.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

schedulerProperties.label: consumer,scheduler
schedulerProperties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

startScheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
startScheduler.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

timeUnit.label: consumer,scheduler
timeUnit.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

useFixedDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
useFixedDelay.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.
